title: ARR
summary: Annualized recurring revenue from subscription customers.
whyPeCares: PE cares because this KPI gives an early read on growth quality, margin expansion, cash conversion, execution discipline, or exit-story credibility.
goodBadSignals: Good performance shows controlled execution and improving unit economics; bad performance signals leakage, weak process ownership, or a diligence risk requiring deeper segmentation.

articleSections.title: ARR: The North Star of SaaS Enterprise Value
body: Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) is the bedrock of SaaS valuation, representing the predictable and contractual revenue that a business expects to receive every year. In Private Equity, ARR is the primary metric we use to determine the 'Scale' and 'Velocity' of a software asset. Unlike one-time professional services or hardware sales, ARR provides the visibility needed to support high leverage and aggressive reinvestment. Our goal as Operating Partners is to ensure that the ARR reported is 'high-quality'—meaning it is tied to multi-year contracts with low churn risk and high contribution margins.

We distinguish between 'Gross ARR' and 'Net ARR.' Gross ARR includes all active contracts, while Net ARR accounts for any known churn or contraction that has occurred but hasn't yet hit the P&L. We use Revenue Operations tools like Maxio or Salesforce Revenue Cloud to maintain a single source of truth for ARR, eliminating the 'spreadsheet sprawl' that often plagues mid-market firms. By professionalizing the ARR tracking, we provide the Investment Committee with the confidence to stay aggressive on growth-focused capital allocation.

The math of ARR is the foundation of the 'Revenue Bridge,' which we analyze monthly. A typical bridge walks from the 'Opening ARR' to the 'Closing ARR' by adding New Logo ARR and Expansion ARR, then subtracting Churned ARR and Contraction ARR. If a business starts the year with $20M in ARR, adds $5M in New Logos, expands existing accounts by $2M, but loses $1M to churn and $0.5M to contraction, the Ending ARR is $25.5M. This 27.5% growth rate is the raw material for multiple expansion at exit.
articleSections.callout: ARR is the currency of the SaaS world; every dollar of recurring revenue is a building block for exit enterprise value.

articleSections.title: The ARR Bridge: Deconstructing the Drivers of Growth
body: A sophisticated ARR Bridge is the most powerful diagnostic tool in an Operating Partner's arsenal. We don't just look at the final number; we look at the 'Quality of the Bridge.' High-performing assets derive a significant portion of their growth from 'Expansion ARR'—selling more to existing customers. This is significantly more efficient than 'New Logo' acquisition, as it carries almost zero Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC). If the bridge shows that growth is entirely dependent on new logos while expansion is flat, it's a sign that the product is failing to capture its full 'Value Share.'

We use 'Waterfall' charts in tools like Clari or Mosaic to visualize the ARR Bridge in real-time. This allows us to spot 'Contraction' trends—where customers reduce their seat count or move to lower tiers—before they become full-blown churn. Contraction is often an early warning signal of competitive entry or budget tightening within the customer base. By identifying these 'Leaky' parts of the bridge early, we can deploy Customer Success teams to perform 'Health Checks' and 'Save' the revenue before the contract expires.

The math of the bridge also reveals 'Net Retention.' If your Expansion ARR exceeds your Churned and Contraction ARR, you have 'Positive Net Retention' (NRR > 100%). This is the 'Force Multiplier' for ARR growth. For example, a company with 120% NRR and 10% New Logo growth will grow ARR by 30% annually. A company with 80% NRR needs 50% New Logo growth just to hit the same target. As operators, we prioritize fixing the 'bottom half' of the bridge (retention) before pouring more capital into the 'top half' (sales).

articleSections.title: ARR Quality: From 'Booked' to 'Committed'
body: Not all ARR is created equal. We look for 'Contractual ARR' that is backed by legally binding multi-year agreements, ideally with 'Automatic Renewal' clauses and 'Annual Price Escalators' (e.g., CPI + 3%). We view 'Month-to-Month' recurring revenue as lower quality because it offers zero protection against sudden churn. During diligence and the hold period, we ruthlessly 'scrub' the ARR to remove 'Zombie ARR'—contracts that are still in the system but where the customer has stopped using the product or has signaled an intent to cancel.

To maintain ARR quality, we implement rigorous 'Deal Desk' processes using Salesforce CPQ. This ensures that every new contract meets our standards for term length, payment frequency (ideally annual upfront), and margin. We also look at 'Platform ARR' vs. 'Module ARR.' If a customer only uses one small module of our platform, they are 'fragile.' If they use the entire suite, the ARR is 'sticky.' We track 'Average Revenue Per Account' (ARPA) and 'Product Density' to measure this stickiness and ensure the ARR is defensible.

The math of 'ARR Yield' is another key metric. This is the amount of ARR generated per dollar of Sales & Marketing spend. A high yield indicates a highly efficient 'Go-to-Market' (GTM) engine, while a low yield suggests that the ARR is being 'bought' at an unsustainable cost. Operating Partners use this ratio to determine where to 'step on the gas' and where to 'apply the brakes.' If the ARR Yield is $1.50, every $1M in marketing spend creates $1.5M in ARR—a clear signal to increase the budget and accelerate toward the exit.

articleSections.title: Operationalizing ARR: Alignment Across the Organization
body: Building a durable ARR engine requires total alignment between Sales, Customer Success, and Product. We move the organization away from 'Bonus on Booking' toward 'Bonus on ARR Realization.' This means sales reps are incentivized not just to sign a contract, but to ensure the customer is successfully onboarded and actually starts generating revenue. We use tools like Gainsight to bridge the gap between 'Closed Won' in the CRM and 'Active ARR' in the P&L, ensuring a smooth handoff from Sales to CS.

Product teams are also tied to the ARR target through 'Usage-Based' triggers. If the product is designed to encourage expansion—for example, by charging per gigabyte of data or per transaction—the ARR grows automatically as the customer succeeds. This creates a 'Flywheel' effect where the product itself becomes the primary driver of the ARR Bridge. We monitor these usage patterns in tools like Pendo or Mixpanel to identify 'Power Users' who are ripe for an upsell and 'Idle Users' who are at risk of contraction.

The math of 'ARR Per Head' is our primary efficiency benchmark. In the early stages, we expect $150k-$200k in ARR per employee; as the business scales toward an exit, we push for $300k+. This requires aggressive automation of the back office and a highly efficient sales force. By keeping the organization lean and focused on ARR growth, we maximize the EBITDA margin and ensure that the revenue is highly profitable. This is the difference between a 'Venture' asset that burns cash and a 'Private Equity' asset that generates a return.

articleSections.title: Exit Readiness: Defending the ARR Multiplier
body: As we prepare for the exit, the ARR becomes the most scrutinized figure in the 'Data Room.' Potential buyers will hire 'Third-Party Diligence' firms to perform a 'Revenue Bridge' audit and a 'Churn Study.' We prepare for this by performing a 'Sell-Side ARR Audit' 12 months out, ensuring that every dollar of ARR is tied to a current, valid contract and that our 'Retention' data is bulletproof. We use tools like Intacct to ensure our revenue recognition (ASC 606) is audit-ready and beyond reproach.

Buyers pay a premium for 'Growth Persistence'—the ability of the ARR to continue growing at its historical rate. We provide a 'Visibility Model' that shows exactly how much of next year's growth is already 'baked in' through current contracts and known expansion pipelines. By showing a 'High-Confidence' path to the next $10M of ARR, we justify a higher multiple. We also highlight the 'Uncapped' nature of our usage-based ARR, giving the buyer a clear 'Up-Side' story that they can use to justify their own investment thesis.

The final act is the 'ARR Multiple Defense.' If the market is paying 8x for 20% growth and 12x for 30% growth, our job is to show the buyer exactly how we can move from 20% to 30% through surgical pricing or expansion playbooks. We present a clean, growing ARR base that is free of 'one-time' noise and 'customer concentration' risk. By delivering a 'High-Quality ARR Asset,' we ensure a competitive bidding process and maximize the MOIC for our LPs. ARR is the foundation of the deal, and its defense is the Operating Partner's ultimate responsibility.
